threads.body: This health check does not actually enforce yellow readiness. Elasticsearch returns HTTP 200 with `"timed_out": true` when `wait_for_status=yellow` expires, so `curl --fail` exits successfully and `ExecWaitStrategy` can proceed while the cluster is still red. Pipe the response through a check for `"timed_out":false` (or a yellow/green status), and update the readiness test to assert that command.

threads.body: The `<8` guard only applies to the node image, but `elasticsearch-rest-client` shares the `elasticsearch-clients` version reference with the Transport Client artifacts in `libs.versions.toml:20-22`. Renovate can therefore bump that shared reference to an 8.x/9.x REST client release, leaving the transport artifacts at nonexistent coordinates and breaking dependency resolution. Apply the same guard to the REST client (or split and pin the version references).

Addressed in d5b3cae12597d4e87d7f6d133065354a2773924b.

Analysis: Renovate updates the shared `elasticsearch-clients` version through the REST Client because that artifact continues past 7.17. Applying the existing `<8` rule to the REST Client prevents that shared reference from moving beyond the Transport Client artifacts' final release line.

Upsides: Renovate can still update all three clients together within 7.x, but it cannot select an 8.x or 9.x REST Client version that breaks Transport Client dependency resolution.

Downsides: The shared client version must remain on 7.x until the Transport Client scenarios are removed or the version references are split.

`http.response.status_code` isn't part of the Elasticsearch span convention - it uses `db.response.status_code` (conditionally required), and the index goes to `db.collection.name`. data.json shows the client emits neither, so asserting the HTTP attribute locks in non-semconv behavior. Maybe drop it and let the gap show up?

            http.request.method: POST
